Celestial Navigation & Sextant
So one week ago I returned to Navarone from a multi-day passage of 600 NM, that took me as far as 180 NM North West, 125 NM North and 150 NM West of Navarone. I have found nothing except for water, of course :-) but my primary goal was not an exploration of the ocean NW of Navarone, but a celestial navigation refresher training before the upcoming real life passage. It went well, although I made several mistakes and errors. I took tens of sights, for tens of running fixes, Meridian transits, Latitude from Polaris and some star fixes.
The only frustrating thing was that we do not have a sextant in eSail, so I had to use an external application called Astron [(https://friendsofthevigilance.org.uk/Astron/Astron.html)](https://steamcommunity.com/linkfilter/?u=http%3A%2F%2F%28https%3A%2F%2Ffriendsofthevigilance.org.uk%2FAstron%2FAstron.html%29). For each sight  I took, I had to manually enter coordinates found in the upper right corner of the eSail into the application, so it added a lot of complexity and work, as well as significantly increased the potential to make mistakes. Nevertheless it was a valuable experience. It would have been much better and more fun if only we had at least a sort of sextant tool in eSail like the CelNav for MSFS [(https://flightsim.to/file/17738/celnav-for-msfs-celestial-navigation-sextant)](https://steamcommunity.com/linkfilter/?u=http%3A%2F%2F%28https%3A%2F%2Fflightsim.to%2Ffile%2F17738%2Fcelnav-for-msfs-celestial-navigation-sextant%29).
So here comes my request to the Producer to add a sextant to the eSail and here are my ideas about it, with increasing level of sophistication and work involved:
1\. As a minimum publish please an API for talented guys like hildaer to make an external sextant tool, like he did for Sailaway (or the one for the MSFS). Otherwise...
2\. Make the sextant available in the game as a pop-up window (like the Moving Map, or Sandbox options). Players should be able to enter IE value and He (height of eye) value, and select a celestial body of interest from a drop-down list. Players should be able to write down Hs and UTC time of observation. A pause button could make it easier. Its look should be similar to how the GPS Anti-Spoof app screen looks like [(http://reednavigation.com/GPSantiSpoof/)](https://steamcommunity.com/linkfilter/?u=http%3A%2F%2F%28http%3A%2F%2Freednavigation.com%2FGPSantiSpoof%2F%29).
3\. Make a sextant tool (similar to binoculars and hand bearing compass). To get the Hs player would have to point it to a celestial body (or its upper or lower limb in case of Sun and Moon) to get the instant readout of Hs. Of course it is not possible to accurately measure Hs with such a tool in the game, so this is the only way - anyway, one needs to play a bit with a real sextant to learn how to measure angles with it...  It would require the better celestial bodies simulation, true-to-life, so Hc and Zn of all celestial nav bodies are always correct, considering location and UTC, unlike today. Similar to Stellarium but not necessarily of so high fidelity. The advantage would be for a player to learn the navigation stars, because he/she would never see the star's name in the eSail sky when taking a sight, unlike in Stellarium.
4\. Add an animation of measuring Hs with a sextant, for example including swinging the sextant in an arc to get true vertical angle. Just a demonstration for educational purposes.
5\. A sextant tool could also be used to measure not only height of celestial bodies but could be used to determine distance by measuring height (vertical angle) of certain terrestrial objects like lighthouses, and using horizontal angles between various objects for the purpose of for example determining a fix by the Snellius method. But I understand it could be troublesome to recreate in eSail.
6\. The highest level of sophistication calls for some new destinations located far away from Shearwater, Navarone and Water Head, say between 50 and 500 NM. It could be just small islands like the Miller Island or the smaller of the two Water Head islands, or even something like Frazer-Arch Shoals. They should not feature high elevation terrain so one would need to get rather close to be able to see them. Would be nice if one could find a jetty or at least an anchorage there.
I understand that I am asking for a lot, but celestial navigation to me has always been an inseparable part of offshore sailing. Having said that, I would say Level 2 above would be satisfactory for me.
P.S. BTW, I would appreciate if it was possible for a player to hide Latitude & Longitude displayed in the upper right corner, by selecting an appropriate option in the Settings.

Thank you.
Let me add two things that could be implemented:
1\. A random error (with a range of, let's say, 0.2-3.0') could be generated for each sight taken, depending on the state of the sea.
2\. Regarding above mentioned sophistication level #3, of course height of only those celestial bodies that are visible to the observer could be measured. Also horizon needs to be visible. So no taking sights at night, stars are not visible in daylight, celestial bodies hidden behind a mountain or behind clouds can not be used, etc.
